description:
One reusable security workflow blocks pull requests and the release workflow on audit installation, data-source, or advisory failure.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The security workflow runs on pull requests and through `workflow_call`, installs a pinned `cargo-audit` with `--locked`, and executes `cargo audit -D warnings` plus both `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=info` commands against the committed locks.
- [hard] REQ-02: Installation, registry, database, and finding failures each propagate as a job failure; the workflow contains no `continue-on-error`, shell fallback, blanket ignore, or advisory allowlist.
- [hard] REQ-03: The shared workflow-contract checks assert that each of the three audit boundaries is a `needs` predecessor of every job a calling workflow runs of its own, so no caller reaches a later job while one of them fails. Binding the release workflow to that assertion is `f9af9788` REQ-02 and REQ-09, evaluated against the release workflow that issue writes rather than the superseded one it deletes.

## Notes

Blast radius: `.github/workflows/security-audit.yml` plus the assertions it declares to the shared workflow-contract harness. Gate-preset examples in `.jit/` remain repository-local configuration examples, not a substitute for the hosted check.


## Scope boundary

This issue makes the three audit boundaries blocking and states their caller
obligation once, on the security workflow, so any workflow that calls it is
bound to reach its own jobs only through that call. Wiring a publication path to
that call belongs to `f9af9788`, which owns `.github/workflows/release.yml` and
replaces the superseded packaging workflow in a single change. Running the
reusable security workflow against the tagged commit before any artifact is
built is that issue's REQ-02, evaluated against the workflow it writes rather
than the one it deletes.
title: Enforce reusable blocking dependency audits
